new_lead.title: HHS Digital Stockpile & Manufacturing Response Network Challenge
verified_facts: The official challenge host still lists Phase 1 submissions due August 28, 2026 at 8 PM; the fetched timeline does not state a timezone, so no timezone is inferred.
Total prize pool is up to $2.04 million across three phases.
Phase 1 requires an 8-page PDF submission paper, a pitch video no longer than 3 minutes, and a conceptual blueprint no longer than 2 pages; all three components are required.

The host explicitly states that AI-generated content is not allowed for narrative development and is not allowed for video development; a member of the submitting team must be visible throughout the submission video.

Up to eight Phase 1 finalists receive $5,000 each and are invited to a hybrid in-person/virtual pitch event at ASPR headquarters in Washington, DC; up to three pitch-event winners receive $150,000 each.
Phase 2 provides two $75,000 developmental milestone prizes per advancing team, up to $150,000 total milestone payments per team; Phase 3 has a total prize purse up to $1.1 million.

Individual prize eligibility requires age 18+ and U.S. citizenship or permanent residency; organizations must be U.S.-incorporated with a primary U.S. place of business; a team lead must be 18+ and a U.S. citizen/permanent resident.
Federal entities or federal employees acting within scope are ineligible, and similar government funding can restrict eligibility.
Judging uses a 1-to-5 Strongly Disagree-to-Strongly Agree scale across published Systems Innovation, Adoptability, Traceability and Scalability, Key Feature Impact, and Presentation criteria.
Solutions are provided to the U.S. Government under unlimited rights as described in FAR 52.227-14 and NFS 1852.227-14; prize-funded work is subject to the same stated unlimited-rights framework.
Prize taxes, expenses, costs, and fees are the winners' responsibility, and the participant agreement contains broad release, indemnification, and hold-harmless terms.

The Phase 1 finalist pitch event is described as hybrid, so in-person travel is not established as mandatory by the reviewed host text; no travel-reimbursement commitment was identified in the reviewed rules.
